public_rationale: The evaluation published May 16, 2025 found that executing generated Python substantially improved localization results but generally worsened tracking results, with significant errors from generated algorithms [e1]. For o3-mini, code assistance sometimes increased error by up to 354% [e1]. This supports the claim that generated Python did not by itself ensure dependable correctness across the tested tasks, despite substantial benefits on some tasks [e1].
limitations: The decisive evaluation covers spatiotemporal tasks; it does not establish unreliability in every Python application [e1].
The reported metrics measure numerical error, not a universal task-completion success rate; exact experiment dates are not supplied [e1].
Successful Hanoi demonstrations were preliminary, used Lua, and were reported June 16, 2025, after the January 1–June 7 observation window [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs writing Python code to supplement their weaknesses is not reliable.

statement.excerpt: In the best case (not always reached) they can write python code, supplementing their own weaknesses with outside symbolic code, but even this is not reliable.

from_speaker: supplementing their own weaknesses with outside symbolic code
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that generating and executing Python does not by itself make LLM solutions dependably correct across tasks.
Reliable does not mean mathematically perfect. Material, recurring errors matter; isolated failures would be insufficient.
Useful code generation and substantial performance improvements are compatible with this claim.
Use calendar 2025 through June 7 for contemporary capability reports because the statement gives no period and this field has no standard reporting interval.
criteria.support_condition: Execution-based evaluations show material errors or unstable task performance when contemporary LLMs use generated Python to solve verifiable problems.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, representative execution-based evaluations show dependably correct task completion using generated Python, without material correction or task-specific intervention.

evidence.explanation: Executed Python improved localization substantially but worsened tracking; the study attributes significant errors to generated algorithms and optimization inaccuracies. This supports the limited claim that adding Python does not assure dependable solutions.

Preliminary demonstrations found successful Hanoi solutions when models generated Lua functions. This cautions against treating puzzle-output failures as proof that code generation cannot help, but it concerns another language and later tests.
